title: Best Badminton Shoes in India (2026)
summary: Three badminton shoes sold in India, for first-timers to serious players. A buying guide built from shop and maker pages, not hand-tested.
description: Three badminton shoes to consider in India, who each suits and what to check before buying. Based on shop and maker pages, not hand-tested.
lead: Which badminton shoes are worth a look in India? This guide covers three: one for first-timers, one for regular players and one for serious players. None of them was hand-tested. Everything here comes from shop and maker pages, and we say clearly what we could not confirm.

picks.name: Kuikma BS 190 (Decathlon India)
picks.label: For first-timers
picks.verdict: A simple first court shoe from Decathlon with a good shop rating, but the India pages leave out many details.
paragraphs: The Kuikma BS 190 is a badminton shoe from Decathlon's own brand. On Decathlon India it comes in Grey and Navy Blue, plus a separate BS 190 Strap version. The India pages say very little about how it is built or who it is for. Placing it here for first-timers is our own judgement.

Here is what to know before buying. The India pages show about 4.5 out of 5 from a few hundred buyers, and a 2-year warranty. No written review comments were visible. Return terms differ between the Grey and Navy pages, so check the exact colour page. Weight, upper material, box contents and the sizing basis (UK or India) are not listed. We could not confirm that the sole is non-marking. Stock by size showed as still loading, so check that too.
good: Decathlon India shows about 4.5 out of 5 from a few hundred buyers
The pages show a 2-year warranty and mention easy returns on at least one colour
It is sold in more than one colour, plus a strap version
not_good: No weight or material details on the India pages, so you cannot judge how light or cushioned it is
Return terms differ by colour page: Grey shows 30-day returns, Navy shows both 'Non returnable' and 'Easy Returns'
Sizes are limited and differ by colour, and the non-marking sole is not confirmed

picks.name: Yonex Power Cushion Cascade Drive 2
picks.label: For regular players
picks.verdict: A comfort-focused Yonex shoe for people who play often, though model codes can be confusing.
paragraphs: The Cascade Drive 2 is also sold as the SHB Cascade Drive 2 or the 2nd gen. Yonex says it is built for stability, comfort and smooth direction changes. It names Power Cushion+, a double Raschel mesh upper, an inner bootie and a toe-assist shape. An Indian retailer calls it an all-round shoe with soft inner cushioning, suited to intermediate and advanced players. These are the maker's and the retailer's words, not independent findings. The tier here is our own judgement, not a shop label.

Amazon.in has a Cascade Drive listing, but its page did not open for us, so we cannot confirm what it shows. We also could not confirm weight, whether the sole is non-marking, warranty, return window or any buyer rating. Yonex has sold older versions, such as the Cascade Drive 1 EX, with different model codes. Match the model code carefully on the listing. The Indian retailer page we opened showed sold out.
good: Yonex describes it as made for stability and comfort (the maker's claim)
An Indian retailer describes soft inner cushioning and a hard-wearing outer
The toe-assist shape is meant to give extra foot support (the maker's claim)
An Amazon.in listing exists, so it should be easy to find and compare
not_good: No weight on the pages we could read, so lightness cannot be judged
Several versions are sold in India with different model codes, which makes comparing hard
Likely more shoe than someone who plays only now and then needs

picks.name: Yonex Power Cushion Aerus Z
picks.label: For serious players
picks.verdict: A very light Yonex shoe for fast footwork, but we could not confirm it is in stock in India right now.
paragraphs: The Aerus Z is Yonex's light, fast shoe. Yonex says it weighs about 240 g per shoe (men's 26.0 cm). It also lists Power Cushion+ in the heel and a graphite sheet in the sole to limit twisting. Yonex offers men's, women's and wide models. All of this is the maker's claim. The premium tier here is our own judgement.

Here is what to know. An Indian retailer lists 250 g and a different sole name, so more than one version may exist. The Indian retailer pages we opened showed sold out, with only two sizes left. We could not confirm that Amazon.in or Flipkart sell it now, so no store button is shown. We also could not confirm a non-marking sole, warranty, return terms or any Indian buyer rating.
good: Yonex aims it at fast footwork and low weight (the maker's claim)
A cushioned heel and a graphite sole sheet are meant for stability (the maker's claim)
A wide model is offered for broader feet (per Yonex)
At least one Indian retailer lists it in several colours
not_good: Premium tier, so it is more shoe than a beginner or casual player needs
Weight and sole description differ between Yonex and the Indian retailer, so versions may vary
The Indian pages we opened were sold out, and warranty and returns are not shown

choose.heading: Look for a non-marking sole
choose.text: Many indoor courts do not allow shoes that leave marks, and dark rubber soles can do that. None of the three shoes here had 'non-marking' stated for that exact model on the pages we read. Ask the seller before you buy.

choose.heading: Match the shoe to how often you play
choose.text: If you play now and then, a basic shoe is usually enough. If you play often, you may want more cushioning and support.

choose.heading: Do not use running shoes
choose.text: Badminton shoes are made for side steps and quick stops and starts. Running shoes are built for moving forward and usually have a taller, less steady sole.

choose.heading: Check the size carefully
choose.text: Sizing changes by brand. A UK shop page for another Yonex shoe says Yonex shoes tend to fit small. Read the size chart, check the return terms, or try the shoe in a store.

choose.heading: Weight is a trade-off
choose.text: Lighter shoes suit fast footwork. Heavier ones often add cushioning and durability. Indian listings often leave out weight. For the Aerus Z, Yonex shows 240 g and an Indian retailer shows 250 g.

choose.heading: Read warranty, returns and stock on the exact listing
choose.text: The same model can have different return terms on different colour pages, as with the BS 190. Stock also changes fast: the Yonex pages we opened in India were sold out. Confirm sizes and availability first.

faq.q: Can I play badminton in running shoes?
faq.a: It is better not to. Running shoes are made for forward movement and usually have a taller, less steady sole. Badminton shoes are made for side steps and quick stops.

faq.q: What is a non-marking sole and why does it matter?
faq.a: It is a sole that does not leave dark marks on the floor. Many indoor courts expect it. None of the three shoes here had it confirmed on the pages we read, so ask the seller.

faq.q: Should a beginner buy a Yonex shoe?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Someone just starting out can begin with a basic shoe like the Kuikma BS 190. A more cushioned or lighter shoe makes more sense once you play often.
